name: CYGNUS
summary: CYGNUS is an international collaboration and planning framework for a distributed network of directional nuclear-recoil observatories, encompassing regional R&D programmes. The overall concept must not be counted alongside its member prototypes as multiple completed detectors.
detection_principle: Low-pressure gas TPCs record recoil energies and directions. The different directions of the Galactic dark-matter wind and solar neutrinos can alleviate background degeneracies in energy-only measurements.

status.label: Proposed
status.evidence: The 2020 feasibility report and 2024 solar-neutrino study discuss future network capabilities; neither reports operation of a completed thousand-cubic-metre detector.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.
